unstated.behaviour: The person is held per browser in a signed HttpOnly cookie (still_session). Two browsers keep two people; all tabs of one browser share one person, and an open tab follows a Continue as in another tab on its next 700 ms poll.
unstated.evidence: Playwright, two contexts: A Continue as Maya + send "hello from Maya", B Continue as Theo + send "hello from Theo"; after reloads A showed Maya with only her messages, B Theo with only his; a further send from A landed in Maya's conversation and B still showed Theo only. Two tabs of A: tab 2 Switch person -> Continue as Ana; tab 1 (no reload) switched to Ana with an empty conversation within 1.2 s, and after reload stayed Ana.
unstated.test_name: TC-2 restores profile, bot and conversation and retries the same message

unstated.behaviour: Every request is checked on the server against the signed cookie; actions use ids only inside the caller's own workspace, so another person's ids return 404 and change nothing.
unstated.evidence: HTTP as Ana with Maya's botId/conversationId/proposal id/memory id: selectConversation 404, decideProposal confirm 404, editMemory 404, forgetMemory 404, send into Maya's conversation 404; Ana's /api/state contains none of Maya's ids or memory; afterwards Maya's proposal still pending, memory ["likes tea"], "what is the status of ORD-1001" -> open. Forged cookie maya.000... and a cookie with the person id swapped to theo -> chooser only; no cookie -> 401; foreign Origin -> 403; foreign Host -> 403.
unstated.test_name: TC-6 commits approvals once, detects stale proposals, and restores results

unstated.behaviour: The first screen holds only the three Continue as buttons; no Setup and no chat controls. Setup appears after a person continues (Message read-only, Send disabled until a token is saved). Saving a token needs a chosen person (401 before). After Switch person a reload stays on the chooser.
unstated.evidence: Playwright, empty data, no token: buttons ["Continue as Maya","Continue as Theo","Continue as Ana"], Setup absent, Message absent. Continue as Maya: Setup visible, Message readOnly true, Send disabled. Save sk-local-short -> alert "The provider refused that token. Check the format and try again.", field cleared; save sk-local-abcdefghijkl -> Setup gone, page HTML has no token. Switch person + reload -> chooser buttons only, no Message box.
unstated.told_where: README "Start": open the app and choose a person, then enter the token in Setup
unstated.test_name: TC-1 validates setup and never projects a saved credential

unstated.behaviour: A valid PROVIDER_TOKEN wins over a saved one; Setup is hidden while it is set, and a setup action then returns 200 without saving. The environment token is not copied to the data folder; with it unset the app is unconfigured until a token is saved, and a saved token is used after that. Which source wins is not stated to the user.
unstated.evidence: HTTP: PROVIDER_TOKEN=sk-local-abcdefghijkl -> configured true, "who are you" -> "I am Assistant. I have no special instructions."; setup with sk-local-zzzzzzzzzzzzzz -> 200, workspace.json token "" (not saved). Restart with variable set -> reply works; restart unset -> configured false, send -> 400 "Save a provider token in Setup before sending."; saved zzz token -> replies work; restart with both -> configured true, file holds only the saved token. No sk-local text in any /api/state.
unstated.test_name: TC-1 validates setup and never projects a saved credential

unstated.behaviour: A refused PROVIDER_TOKEN is treated as unsaved: Setup shows with an alert that the environment token was refused (without showing it) and a new token can be saved; sends are refused until then.
unstated.evidence: PROVIDER_TOKEN=not-a-token: GET / 200, state configured false, environmentTokenRefused true, token text absent. PROVIDER_TOKEN=sk-local-short, Continue as Maya: send "hello" -> 400 "Save a provider token in Setup before sending."; save sk-local-bad -> 400 "The provider refused that token..."; save sk-local-abcdefghijkl -> 200 and "hello" replied. A saved token cannot stop being accepted (the stand-in checks format only).
unstated.told_where: README "What to expect" > Setup: refused PROVIDER_TOKEN, Setup says so without showing it
unstated.test_name: TC-14 tells setup that the environment token was refused without showing it

unstated.behaviour: Token stored in plain text in DATA_DIR/workspace.json (file mode 600, folder 700); never sent in any response, and token-shaped text in messages is replaced by "[provider token hidden]". The provider-error path logs nothing. But when workspace.json is damaged, startup crashes and Node prints the start of the file, including the saved token, to the server output.
unstated.evidence: Setup + "hello [fail once]" + Retry: alert text "The reply failed. Retry to resume without sending your message again.", no token in state or server output; "my token is sk-local-..." stored/echoed as "[provider token hidden]"; file holds token once. Then truncated workspace.json by 5 bytes and ran node server.js: exit 1, output begins "<anonymous_script>:1 {\"version\":4,\"token\":\"sk-local-abcdefghijkl\"..." (token printed).
unstated.test_name: TC-1 validates setup and never projects a saved credential

spec_notes: The specification decides many of the unstated points in ordinary requirement lines without marking them as the builder's choices: browser-specific sessions (U-1), Use copying an instruction (U-17), interrupted tasks not resuming on their own (U-41), resume-at-failed-step (U-42), discarding in-flight output on cancel (U-43), conflict on a changed from-value or a taken order id (U-33, U-34), and a Since-you-were-away summary on reload (U-44). Nothing is marked open for the customer. "Edit loads the entry and updates it under its name" reads as if the name cannot change, while the product renames the item. It pins "Maya sees three orders" and the exact preview text, which hold only for the starting records. It is silent on token precedence, duplicate names, value validation, ORD-id prefix matches, damaged or unwritable data and operator logging.
tests_notes: TC-2, TC-6 and TC-7 each cover many behaviours at once (TC-7: steer, failure, retry, cancel, restart and reply interruption; TC-6: cross-person refusal, concurrent confirms, stale and competing proposals, restart). Tests tied to internals: TC-15 regex-matches app.js source text, TC-20 regex-matches CSS rules, TC-8 matches raw HTML attribute strings, TC-12 reads workspace.json and its internal shape (users.maya.bots[0].conversations[0]), TC-1 expects 401 for setup before choosing a person and an incrementing version field. All HTTP tests use this build's private action names and state shape, so they would fail on another correct build. TC-7 relies on timing (delay(800) expecting Completed with STANDIN_STEP_MS=140). TC-9/TC-11 assert exact refusal wording. No test covers duplicate bot names, the shared instruction library across bots, damaged data, or the Since-you-were-away rules.
maintainer: lib/workspace.js puts every action in one switch inside a whole-state copy-and-rename transaction, and background replies and tasks re-find their targets by ids and runId on each step; the "unsaved marks" (stalled/settle) that replay failure states into views until storage recovers are subtle and easy to break. In public/app.js the generation/version guards, fingerprinted re-rendering and focus restoration are intertwined, so changing what a list shows can silently change where focus lands or drop a stale update.
